To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the identification of coding potential from random sequence reads is possible, that the identification is best achieved with a new sequence masking technique, and that this technique can be used to streamline the random sequencing strategy.

the random sequencing strategy can be streamlined by using a 2.5- to 3-fold sequencing redundancy and that the identification of coding sequences from the raw data is possible with a computer-based approach.
the identification of coding sequences in genomic DNA is facilitated by the following three new developments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of human genes, particularly those associated with human disease.
the development and application of new methods for the identification of coding regions in large-scale genomic sequencing projects.
the development of new bioinformatics tools for the analysis of large genomic sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the streamlined random sequencing approach is a powerful strategy to identify coding exons in the genomic sequence, and that this method can be used to identify the gene responsible for a disease,

a random sequencing approach is not necessarily the best way to identify exons in the human genome, and a more efficient strategy is possible, provided that the raw sequencing data are analyzed appropriately.
, if the primary goal of the project is the identification of coding sequence, the random sequencing strategy can be greatly optimized, and the usual 8-fold redundancy can be reduced to 3- to 4-fold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identification of coding sequences from the raw data is possible, but only after a careful masking of the noncoding sequences.
the random sequencing strategy can be used for the identification of exons, provided that the computer analysis of raw sequence data is optimized.
the coding potential of a genomic region can be determined from a 3-fold redundancy of random shotgun sequencing data, without prior subcloning and with a 2.5% false-positive rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of coding regions, the random sequencing strategy can be optimized for the identification of coding potential.
a new sequencing strategy, based on computer-assisted detection of coding exons, is possible.
the sequencing of the human genome will be more efficient and cost-effective if coding exons are identified as soon as the raw data are generated.
